Museum of Lost Space Technology is an interactive educational website that brings the stories of four pieces of NASA equipment left on the Moon to life: the Lunar Module Descent Stage, Lunar Roving Vehicle, Apollo 11 Passive Seismic Experiment, and Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector.

Through first-person storytelling adapted to different age groups, visitors can hear the stories of these objects from their own perspectives. The experience also features interactive illustrative 3D models and accessible scientific explanations of each object's design, purpose, and operation.

By combining storytelling, 3D exploration, and scientific information, the project makes space exploration more engaging and accessible to school-age audiences. It reveals how equipment left behind on the lunar surface contributed to scientific discoveries and reminds us that even when a mission ends, its legacy is not forgotten.
details:
🌕 Museum of Lost Space Technology

The Museum of Lost Space Technology is an interactive educational website that explores the history of NASA equipment left on the lunar surface. It transforms these objects into opportunities to learn about space exploration, engineering, and scientific discoveries.

The first version focuses on four pieces of equipment: the Lunar Module Descent Stage, the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), the Apollo 11 Passive Seismic Experiment, and the Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector.

🚀 How It Works

The website combines two main experiences:

📖 Interactive Narrative: Visitors explore the history of each object through a digital book guided by a narrator, learning about its purpose, operation, historical context, and scientific contributions.

🛰️ 3D Exploration: Interactive illustrative models allow visitors to examine the equipment from different angles and better understand its structure and functions.

The narratives are adapted for different age groups, including children and adults, adjusting the language and scientific complexity to make the content accessible to a wider audience.

🎓 Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes the history of lunar exploration more accessible and engaging by combining storytelling, scientific information, and interactive 3D visualization.

Its main goal is to spark curiosity and encourage learning about astronomy, engineering, space technology, and scientific research, especially among students and young space enthusiasts.

The content is based on historical, technical, and scientific documentation, including NASA publications and Apollo mission records, helping ensure that the educational experience remains connected to reliable historical information.

🎨 Creativity and Design Considerations

The project's creative approach lies in transforming abandoned lunar equipment into interactive storytelling experiences. Instead of presenting these objects solely through photographs or technical documents, the website allows visitors to discover their stories through narration and 3D exploration.

During development, the team prioritized:

  • Clear, age-appropriate language without compromising scientific accuracy.
  • Different levels of detail to accommodate diverse audiences.
  • A digital book format for progressive storytelling.
  • Interactive 3D models to complement scientific explanations.
  • Historical and technical documentation as the foundation for the content.

The initial scope was limited to four lunar objects to allow for greater depth and a more cohesive experience. The 3D models are illustrative rather than exact technical reconstructions.

💻 Technologies and Tools

The project was developed using web technologies and 3D rendering tools:

  • HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+): Website structure, styling, logic, and interactions.
  • SVG: Vector graphics.
  • Three.js and WebGL: Interactive 3D models and browser-based rendering.
  • HTML5 Canvas 2D API: Two-dimensional graphics and simulations.
  • Web Audio API and HTML5 Audio: Audio processing and playback.
  • Microsoft Edge Neural TTS and Python (edge-tts): Narration generation using neural text-to-speech technology.
  • Web Speech API: Browser-based speech features.
  • Git: Source code version control.
  • Artificial Intelligence (AI): We use AI tools, such as Google Gemini, to assist with and improve code, as well as to generate narrative audio.
